scope: Manufacturing/Production, OEE, Supply Chain, Procurement Planning, Dispatch Planning, Shipment Operations
method: Read-only source audit of enabled sidebar definitions, literal routes, forms, state transitions, lookup calls, API services and selected SQL contracts. No application changes, backend start, database queries, mutations, or live browser testing were performed by this reviewer. A follow-up reconciliation checked grouped Manufacturing, ProductionWorkspace, BOM effectivity, PackagingConversion, SupplyChain, Procurement, Dispatch and Shipment controllers against nested UI/service calls.
classification: Screens and routes are not master counts. Nested forms, child configuration, transactions, reports and role views are explicitly classified below.

findings.title: Daily typed quantities have no unsaved-work protection
findings.observation: Daily drafts use component useState. Links to individual orders/new order/planning and route changes exist, but this component has no beforeunload/route guard or persistence. Navigating away and unmounting or reloading discards entered but unreviewed rows.
findings.proposal: Add a visible unsaved count, scoped recoverable draft storage or router leave guard, and explicit Discard; scope by authenticated user/company/order version and never auto-post recovered data.
findings.benefit: Prevents a worker losing many typed/pasted rows and guessing what was saved.
findings.verification: Source behavior; navigation/reload reproduction should be tested in browser before delivery.

findings.kind: source-confirmed incomplete lookup behavior at larger data sizes
findings.title: Several selectors and repair queues only load the first 200 records
findings.observation: Manual shipment loads only page 1 of Items and packaging profiles; plan-based shipment loads first 200 finalized runs; OEE daily resources first 200; BOM repair loads first 200 products and locally searches those products, plus only first 100 BOM versions. Item Manufacturing history loads first 20 legacy production records without history pagination. Larger datasets can make valid records unavailable or falsely look absent. The BOM Issues API itself returns an unpaged collection; its requested PageSize is not evidence of a 200-issue cap.
findings.proposal: Server-backed search with pagination, or deliberately fetch every permitted page where small bounded reference catalogs are intended. Display total and loading/failure states, retain selected inactive records when viewing history.
findings.benefit: Client can find real Items, moulds, runs and BOM issues as their catalog grows.

findings.title: Packaging creation says saved before the nested verification step is discoverable
findings.observation: Packaging create/update shows success and navigates to the list. Verified source-to-base conversion is rendered only for an existing record in edit/view; the profile list presents Units/box/active/default but not conversion readiness. Required downstream evidence may remain unresolved despite successful save.
findings.proposal: After create offer Save & verify conversion; show a profile readiness badge and direct Verify link; show base/source units and a sample conversion. Keep save permission and approval permission separate, handing off to an approver when needed.
findings.benefit: A client completes setup once, instead of discovering an unexplained blocker during import or dispatch.

findings.kind: usability/risk recommendation, not proven stock defect
findings.title: Three production-entry concepts need an explicit business distinction
findings.observation: Manufacturing Daily Production records accepted/rejected quantities and actual material posting; OEE Production Entries records runtime/mould/shots. In addition, Item → Manufacturing still exposes its own legacy Manufacture/draft/post/cancel stock-production transaction. A client can reasonably think an entry satisfies another workflow or enter the same real-world output twice.
findings.proposal: Use one primary Production entry path and clearly separate Daily output & materials from Machine runtime & shots. Route new production work consistently after deciding the supported legacy migration strategy, retain legacy history, add related order/reading links where valid, and show explicit stock-effect labels. Do not blindly merge APIs or infer stock output from mould cavity.
findings.benefit: Avoids duplicate entry confusion and incorrect expectations about stock and machine reports.

findings.title: OEE Off means skipped; deliberate no-production cannot be acknowledged in this grid
findings.observation: Bulk entry filters only isRunning rows and refuses saving when all machines are off. UI says Off · skipped. An intentionally stopped/no-production day is therefore not evidenced by this form, which can confuse reporting completeness with missing entry.
findings.proposal: Add explicit Not run / Planned stop / Running acknowledgments with reason, preferably a day-completion review. Preserve genuine missing evidence and do not manufacture zero output readings.
findings.benefit: Supervisor knows whether nobody entered data or no production actually occurred.

findings.title: Production detail exposes resource IDs and technical evidence before business names
findings.observation: Order context shows Machine # / Mould # / Shift #, Channel #, BOM/routing IDs/current version, and frozen operations/work centres as IDs/rate basis code. These are useful audit identities but hard for workers to recognize.
findings.proposal: Resolve permitted resource labels or preserve label snapshots; present Item, resource names, due date, remaining and next action first; put IDs/version/calculation basis under Details.
findings.benefit: Fewer wrong-order/resource selections and less training.

findings.title: Finalized dispatch planning does not guide users directly into linked shipment creation
findings.observation: Dispatch detail primary actions end after Finalized and finalization text says it does not create a shipment. Shipment creation requires a separate form, loading finalized runs and choosing the run again; the form has no run query/state prefill in its initial state.
findings.proposal: After finalize expose Create shipment with run/warehouse context, remaining allocations and existing shipments; support a verified deep link and preserve permissions.
findings.benefit: Removes rediscovery and wrong-run selection while retaining a review before shipment creation.

findings.title: Transporter request failures silently become an empty transporter list
findings.observation: Plan-based shipment creation catches transporter list failure and sets []; detail workspace does the same. A permission/network/server failure looks like 'no transporters configured'.
findings.proposal: Independent transporter error/loading/retry state and relevant Party-role setup link when genuinely empty; preserve other form data.
findings.benefit: User fixes the real issue instead of creating duplicate parties or abandoning entry.

findings.title: Operational production report primary export is NDJSON
findings.observation: OperationalReportsPage downloads production-<kind>.ndjson. The client works with sheets, while this output requires data tooling or import steps.
findings.proposal: Offer formatted CSV/XLSX with human headings, units, date/filter basis and quality flags; preserve NDJSON under Advanced export for integrations.
findings.benefit: Client can immediately open, reconcile and share the report in Excel.

findings.title: Policy forms expose many mathematical and logistics fields without a worked outcome
findings.observation: Warehouse priority/sort, packaging dimensions/divisor/effectivity/defaults, dispatch safety/recurring factors/rounding/priority, typed supplier lead duration alongside legacy configured days, and routing rate/quantity basis require users to understand implementation concepts.
findings.proposal: Basic/Advanced sections, sensible named policy presets, live worked example, resolved effective policy summary and Save & next setup actions. Do not create additional masters.
findings.benefit: Faster onboarding and fewer valid-but-wrong configurations.

findings.title: OEE custom modal headings are not connected to the dialog name; editing stays enabled while saving
findings.observation: OEE shared master modal and production quick-create/edit modals omit AppModal title and render their own h2. AppModal then announces only Dialog. Shared master fields disable only isView, and its Cancel button remains enabled while isSubmitting, despite isBusy guarding outer modal closure.
findings.proposal: Pass title or aria-labelledby consistently; disable/edit-freeze inputs and cancel while a request is in flight, or define safe cancellation behavior. Verify keyboard focus/return and announced title.
findings.benefit: Accessible modal identity and less confusion when a save completes after users have changed/closed the form.

findings.title: Cross-module setup and shipment execution need a permission-aware next-action checklist
findings.observation: Order creation lists six lookup permissions and effective prerequisites; shipment execution spans seven tabs, separate packing verification, invoice owner declaration and partial invoice allocations. Most pieces are implemented but a new user must infer the correct sequence.
findings.proposal: Show a small readiness checklist with Ready / Needs setup / Ask approver / Failed to load, business-language reasons, direct repair links and return-to-current-work context. Permission failure must not look like absent master data.
findings.benefit: Client can proceed without knowing the module architecture or asking support where the next screen is.

findings.kind: source-confirmed capability mismatch; live role test still required
findings.title: Legacy Item production Post/Cancel checks Edit in UI but Approve in API
findings.observation: ItemManufacturingTab requests view/create/update capabilities only, and both Post and Cancel/reverse actions are gated by canUpdate. The API explicitly requires Manufacturing.Productions Approve for both operations. An editor without approval sees actions that should fail 403, while an approval-only user may not see the required action.
findings.proposal: Request and use canApprove for stock posting/reversal independently from canUpdate for draft editing; give a clear missing-permission explanation. Verify view-only, create-only, edit-only, approve-only and combined roles.
findings.benefit: Approvers can complete work and editors are not led into predictable failed stock actions.

findings.kind: API-supported command without explicit frontend entry
findings.title: Approved BOM end-effectivity command has no dedicated frontend action
findings.observation: ProductionBomEffectivityController exposes POST boms/{id}/effectivity with Boms Approve. Item Manufacturing only offers effective dates in ordinary BOM editing, edit/delete inactive BOMs, and activate/deactivate. Frontend configuration closeEffectivity calls /configuration/{kind}/{id}/effectivity, whose backend deliberately rejects kind=bom; no call to the dedicated BOM endpoint was found.
findings.proposal: Add a permission-aware End validity date review for active BOM versions, explaining impact on new orders and preserving frozen history. Do not add a separate BOM master.
findings.benefit: Users can safely retire a recipe on a specific business date through the approved flow.

findings.title: Legacy packing recovery requires removing allocations but normal packing offers no removal
findings.observation: The verification UI says remove affected draft package allocations in Packing first; SQL throws REPACK_REQUIRED if existing package-item allocations are present. Packing UI only builds new packages and displays packages; service/controller expose GET suggestions and POST create, not edit/remove. Base Save procedure rejects an existing package number and inserts a new package. The user cannot perform the instructed recovery using the available normal UI/API.
findings.proposal: Implement a controlled draft-only package edit/remove/repack workflow with reconciliation, version/permission checks and audit; expose the action from the blocker. Protect dispatched packages and posted stock. Until supported, guidance should state the actual recovery path rather than link to an unavailable action.
findings.benefit: Clients can fix wrong/legacy packaging without database intervention, abandoned shipments or duplicate packing.

flows: Setup shared Item/Unit/BOM, OEE Machine/Mould, HR Shift → Work Centre + capacity + Operation → Item routing/eligibility → production planning → draft → release/reservation → daily entry/partial material completion → linked correction/report.

Channel → channel Warehouse → shared channel-SKU mapping → packaging profile + verified conversion → dispatch SKU policy → sales/warehouse/inbound committed snapshots → calculate/override/allocate/finalize dispatch run → linked shipment draft.

Procurement sales import/manual source → shared SKU resolution + canonical BOM + purchased Item policy → buy-list/advanced preview → saved draft → adjustment/reason → finalize → sourced supplier/price/tax selection → existing Purchase Order draft.

Shipment draft → verified packing/units + invoice ownership/line allocations → packing/docket/readiness → actual dispatch with physical stock effect → transit/appointment/attempt → receipt outcomes/return receipt → freight approval/payment/Rojmel → reports.
OEE Machine/Mould/Reason → daily runtime/shot readings → grouped history → performance, insights, submission audit and OEE reports; this is distinct from physical stock completion.
strengths: Daily grid and Kanban are implemented and directly discoverable. They are not still missing work.
New stock-affecting production workflows use explicit review, exact quantity handling, versions, request identity/recovery, and authoritative refresh.
Shared master reuse is generally correct; avoid proposing duplicate SKU, Machine, Mould, Shift, BOM, Transporter or stock masters.

Procurement already has consolidated setup tabs, a simple buy-list, advanced four-step planning, editable draft/finalized snapshots, source-preserving PO conversion, and a workbook-like product-channel summary.
Dispatch has a clear lifecycle action, blockers and committed source batches; Shipment has explicit permissions, conflicts and distinct historical import behavior.
Reporting often keeps missing evidence and mixed units explicit rather than showing invented zero totals.
limitations: No live browser, role-based scenario, responsive visual screenshot or accessibility execution proof from this child audit.
No database integration proof and no confirmation that the previously reported company-configuration runtime error is resolved.
No stock posting, reversal, invoice ownership, dispatch-to-shipment or finance action was executed; source intent is not runtime correctness.
No global count of masters is asserted. The coverage rows include routes, transactions, reports, child configurations and role views.
Legacy /reports/manufacturing and shared inventory/Party/HR/admin/general dashboard pages are parent/other-reviewer scope; this audit focuses the owned operational modules.
Backend reconciliation is source-only. Migration files indicate intended contracts; no assertion is made that the live database has applied those migrations.
